input: Bleach and re-grout the kitchen sink area

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: The sink area could mean just the backsplash tiles, the countertop surround, or the floor nearby — the size and surface type dramatically changes the amount of materials and effort required.
The current condition of the grout (mouldy, cracked, crumbling, or just discoloured) determines whether bleaching alone is enough first or if full removal and re-grouting is needed everywhere.
Knowing how much time is available affects whether this is done in one session or split across days, especially since bleaching and grouting each need drying/curing time.
Whether this is a solo DIY job or involves hiring a tradesperson changes the entire plan — tools needed, steps to follow, and budget all shift significantly.
Knowing what tools and materials are already on hand (grout remover, grout float, sealant, bleach pen vs. spray) avoids recommending purchases the user already has.
The desired grout colour and finish (matching existing, going lighter/darker, or switching to epoxy grout) affects which product to buy and the final look.
Understanding whether the goal is purely functional (sealed and clean) or also aesthetic (like-new appearance) determines how thorough the prep and finishing steps need to be.

gold.taskTitle: Bleach and re-grout the kitchen sink area
gold.taskDescription: Clean and restore the grout in the kitchen sink area by bleaching existing grout and applying fresh grout where needed.

questions.title: Which surfaces are included — backsplash, countertop, or both?
questions.description: Identify the exact surfaces in the sink area that need to be bleached and re-grouted, so the scope of materials and effort can be accurately planned.

questions.title: What is the current condition of the grout?
questions.description: Determine whether the grout is simply stained/discoloured, or if it is cracked, crumbling, or mouldy — this dictates how much needs to be removed versus cleaned.

questions.title: Is this a DIY project or will a tradesperson be hired?
questions.description: Clarify who will be doing the work, as this changes the recommended steps, tools, and whether professional products or consumer-grade ones are more appropriate.

questions.title: How much time do you have to complete this project?
questions.description: Understand the available time window, since bleaching, grout removal, re-grouting, and sealing each require drying or curing periods that may span more than one day.

questions.title: What tools or materials do you already have at home?
questions.description: Find out which supplies are already available (bleach, grout float, oscillating tool, sealant, etc.) to avoid redundant purchase recommendations.

questions.title: What grout colour or finish are you aiming for?
questions.description: Determine whether the user wants to match the existing grout colour, go lighter or darker, or switch to a different type such as epoxy grout for durability.

questions.title: Is the priority a like-new look, or just clean and functional?
questions.description: Establish the standard of finish the user expects — a purely functional result requires less prep and finishing detail than a fully restored, aesthetic outcome.
